items.stem: A service control policy (SCP) in AWS Organizations is used to:

options.text: Set the maximum permissions available in member accounts
options.rationale: Correct: SCPs set permission boundaries; they restrict, never grant, access.
SCPs cannot grant access; identity policies do that within SCP limits.
SCPs are about permissions, not networking.
Logging is handled by CloudTrail and log aggregation, not SCPs.

items.explanation: Correct: SCPs set permission boundaries; they restrict, never grant, access.

items.stem: Where should an organization centralise CloudTrail and config logs in a landing zone?

options.rationale: Correct: a separate audit account isolates and protects centralised logs.
Per-account-only logging has no tamper-resistant central copy.
Public exposure of audit logs is a serious security risk.
Audit logs must not live in an unmanaged personal account.

items.explanation: Correct: a separate audit account isolates and protects centralised logs.

items.stem: Which TWO are valid reasons to use multiple AWS accounts? (Select TWO.)

options.rationale: Correct: separate accounts limit the blast radius of mistakes and breaches.

options.text: Clear cost separation by team or environment
options.rationale: Correct: account boundaries make cost attribution clean.
Multiple accounts still require IAM for access control.

options.text: Because one account cannot run more than one service
options.rationale: A single account can run many services; that is not the reason.

items.explanation: Correct: isolation of blast radius and clean cost separation are core reasons for multiple accounts.
